note: Duotone presets: map the photo's luminance to four stops -- dark -> mid -> light -> paper. The light end equals the paper colour (near-white), so large bright areas such as sky and ground melt naturally into the paper -- this is the key step of 'not treating the photo as a background image'. tone_shift varies light/dark within one preset (e.g. darkening the second board of a collage).
method: presets v1 (four control points: 0 -> shadow, 0.45 -> mid, 0.82 -> light, 1.0 -> paper)

azure-gold.desc: Dunhuang azurite + golden brown; the temper of murals and the moon disc

malachite-green.desc: mineral green dominant; calm and clear, suited to landscape subjects

vermilion.desc: the warmth of terracotta red and ochre; suited to festival and folk subjects

ink.desc: near-monochrome, 'ink in five shades'; suited to steles, artefacts and documentary photography

amaranth.desc: the printed temper of pagoda silhouettes and moon discs (see reference case: duotone + paper sky)

umber-gold.desc: ochre-gold tone, warm and heavy; suited to archaeological and artefact subjects
